summary: Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power Limited (NUPPL), KH-419, G.N. Extension, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow - 226010, Uttar Pradesh ** Petitioner** 5. The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 27.1.2025 had filed present Petition, claiming tariff in respect of the entire generating station, i.e. based on the actual COD of Unit-I and the anticipated COD of Units-II and III. After hearing the matter on 8.4.2025 and subsequently on 20.5.2025, the Commission issued its order dated 12.8.2025 in 6. The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 20.2.2026 has filed an IA No. 37/2026 in the present Petition, under provisions of the Regulation 9(1) and Regulation 10 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, from the date of Commercial Operation of Unit-I (i.e., 12.12.2024) and Unit II (9.12.2025) till 31.3.2029, after serving the copies to the Respondents. Accordingly, the annual fixed charges claimed by the Petitioner, are as under: 7. During the hearing, the Petitioner has submitted that Unit-II of the generating station has achieved COD and requested for an interim tariff for the same. The Petitioner also submitted that the interim tariff sought is lower than the interim tariff determined for Unit-I and, thus, is in the interest of the beneficiaries. The Petitioner has further submitted that an Interlocutory Application No. 37 of 2026 has been filed seeking amendment of the Petition for inclusion of Unit-II and for the grant of interim tariff and although the earlier directions provided liberty for filing of a separate Petition, considering that the tariff period is the same and similar practice has been followed in respect of other generating stations, the present amendment has been sought to avoid multiplicity of proceedings. In response to a specific query of the Commission regarding the commissioning of Unit-III, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the same is expected to be achieved by June/July 2026. The learned counsel for the Respondent, UPPCL, has sought liberty to file its reply, postconsolidation and amending the Petition upon COD of the generating station 8. The Commission, after hearing the learned counsels for the parties, directed the Petitioner to submit certain additional information, after serving copies to the Respondents, and also reserved its order, with regard to the prayer of the Petitioner for the grant of an interim tariff for Unit-I and Unit-II of the generating station, in terms of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 9. The Petitioner has prayed for the grant of an interim tariff, equivalent to 90% of the total tariff claimed for Unit-I and Unit-II, for billing purpose, and allow the Petitioner to provisionally charge tariff from its actual date of Commercial Operations as per this Petition, subject to the final determination of the tariff for the generating station by the Commission. The Respondent, UPPCL, sought liberty to file its reply, postconsolidation and amending the Petition upon COD of the generating station. 10. We have considered the submissions made by the parties. In order to enable the Petitioner to meet its ongoing financial obligations through a reasonable recovery of the cost of supply of electricity by the Petitioner to the Respondents and keeping in view that the interim tariff of Unit-I and Unit-II of the generating station will be subject to adjustment, based on the final tariff to be determined by the Commission, we, on prudence check, proceed to examine the prayer of the Petitioner for the grant of interim _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations, the Commission may consider granting an interim tariff of up to ninety per cent (90%) of the tariff claimed in the case of a new generating station or unit thereof or transmission system, or element thereof during the first hearing of the application for billing purposes till the final tariff is determined by the Commission:_ 12. The Petitioner has submitted that it has placed on record the required information in the prescribed format, as per the provisions of the 2024 Tariff 15. The Petitioner has furnished the reasons for the delay of 1477 days in the commissioning of Unit-I, viz., delay due to land acquisition and delay due to other issues and has submitted that these were beyond the control of the Petitioner. Regarding the delay of 1658 days for Unit-II, the Petitioner has submitted that the uncontrollable factors for Unit I had a cascading effect on Unit II also. Apart from this, Unit II also faced further delay due to excessive heavy rainfall and acute financial distress being faced by M/S BGRESL {a key contractor for GA-3 BOP package (covering CHP, AHP, NDCT, Wagon Tipplers, Stacker-Reclaimer and 400 kV GIS)}, whose accounts turned as Non-Performing Assets (NPA) and subsequent initiation of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) for the same. This rendered M/s BGRESL incapable of mobilising the financial and working capital resources necessary for execution of critical project activities. station.
